subject: Follow-up: Mutual action plan & verification for inference availability incident
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Amy Park <amy.park@datelinesys.com>, ops@datelinesys.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, May 27, 2026 at 09:12 AM PDT
Subject: Follow-up: Mutual action plan & verification for inference availability incident

Hi Amy / DataLine ops team,

Thanks again for your time this morning. Per our call, I’m sharing a concise RCA summary, the immediate mitigations we applied, and a proposed mutual action plan (MAP) to verify remediation and avoid recurrence. We want this to be auditable for your compliance team, so I’ve attached the timeline CSV and a small evidence stub.

Executive summary (tl;dr):
- Incident: transient inference availability degradation impacting a subset of customers on the Redwood shared pool between 08:03–08:56 PDT on 2026-05-26.
- Impact to DataLine: increased request timeouts for batch scoring jobs (approx. 4% errors during window).
- Root cause (high-level): cascading KV-cache evictions triggered by a GC spike in a background maintenance job on a subset of serving nodes, which temporarily caused model kernel selection regressions and longer token generation latencies.

Timeline (high level):
- 08:03 PDT: first elevated error rates observed in telemetry and customer alerts.
- 08:12 PDT: automatic failover engaged for affected serve group; partial recovery noticed.
- 08:30 PDT: engineering rollback of recent maintenance job and forced KV-cache warmup; error rate down to baseline.
- 08:56 PDT: service fully stabilized for all affected customers.

Immediate mitigations performed by Redwood:
- Forced eviction-free restart of the maintenance agent on impacted nodes (08:18 PDT).
- Increased temporary KV-cache retention window to prevent thrash during warmup (08:22 PDT).
- Rolling restart of two nodes with abnormal GC profiles (08:35 PDT).

Short RCA detail:
- The maintenance job that rotates model artifacts triggered an unusually long stop-the-world GC on one instance (unrelated to customer traffic). That GC caused a burst of KV-cache evictions across a serve shard. The runtime’s kernel-selection logic prefers smaller-kernel fallbacks when prefix KV cache is cold; with many concurrent connections, this produced longer path lengths and increased tail latency.
- This interaction surfaced only under the specific workload mix and a recent runtime tweak to aggressive cleanup thresholds.

Attachments: rwc-incident-timeline.csv (timeline export), kv-eviction-heapdump.tar.gz (heap dump excerpt), post-incident-evidence-stub.txt

Proposed mutual action plan (short):
1) Verification checklist: Redwood will produce a checklist you can run against your staging environment to validate the fix. Expected delivery: 2026-05-28 EOD. (See attached MAP-DataLine-verification-checklist.xlsx)
2) Telemetry snapshot: we’ll share the filtered request traces and aggregated token-level latencies for your account for the incident window. Expected delivery: 2026-05-28 10:00 PDT.
3) Configuration change: we will roll a conservative KV-cache retention policy and revert the aggressive cleanup thresholds in the next maintenance window. Planned date: 2026-05-30 (non-peak).
4) Joint verification call: we suggest a 30-min call to walk through the checklist and confirm logs. Proposed window: 2026-05-29 10:00–11:00 PDT.

Please let us know if you need a different date/time for the call or if your compliance team needs additional artifacts. I’ll follow up tomorrow with the verification checklist and the exact Drive link for evidence.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Sr. Technical Account Lead | Redwood Inference
(attachment: rwc-incident-timeline.csv)
(attachment: kv-eviction-heapdump.tar.gz)
(attachment: post-incident-evidence-stub.txt)

Thanks, Irene — helpful summary.

A couple quick asks from our side:
- Can you include a short checklist our security/compliance team can use to validate the KV-cache policy change (we're primarily interested in what logs to look for and an expected signal if the change is successful)?
- Will the telemetry snapshot include request ids and sample traces? We may need those for our internal audit.
- For the joint verification, 2026-05-29 10:00 PDT works for our ops and security lead. Please send a calendar invite.

Also confirming the impact window you listed (08:03–08:56 PDT) and that our paid jobs experienced ~4% errors — we will attach a small excerpt of our job logs to the verification ticket.

— Amy Park
Head of Engineering, DataLine Systems
(attachment: dataline-joblog-sample.txt)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Amy Park <amy.park@datelinesys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, May 28, 2026 at 08:45 AM PDT
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Mutual action plan & verification for inference availability incident

Hi Amy — thanks for the quick reply and for confirming the window. Attaching the MAP checklist as promised and the Drive folder with evidence. Below is the concrete verification checklist we propose for your compliance team; the attached spreadsheet expands each step and includes a pass/fail column.

Verification checklist (summary):
1) KV-cache retention verification
   - What to look for: continuous KV cache hit rates during a 30-min warmup following a rolling restart. Expected: sustained >95% hit after initial warmup (within first 5 minutes).
   - Logs: redwood.kv.cache.metrics (hit_rate, eviction_count) + node GC logs.
2) Latency distribution check
   - What to look for: 99th percentile token latency returning to baseline within 20 minutes of failover.
   - Logs: redwood.inference.latency.{p50,p95,p99} filtered to your account id.
3) Request-trace sample validation
   - What to look for: one request id trace showing kernel selection path before and after the fix. We will provide 3 sample traces with request ids.
4) Regression gate for maintenance jobs
   - What to look for: no stop-the-world GC events >250ms during maintenance windows on serve nodes.

Deliverables & owners:
- Redwood: MAP spreadsheet + Drive evidence folder (Irene) — delivered 2026-05-28 08:40 PDT (link below).
- DataLine: run checklist in staging and attach results (Amy) — target 2026-05-29 EOD.
- Joint verification call to confirm pass/fail and discuss rolling policy (Irene, Marissa) — scheduled 2026-05-29 10:00 PDT.

Drive evidence: https://drive.redwood.com/rdw/incident/DL-119-MAP (contains traces, filtered logs, and the timeline CSV).
HubSpot ticket: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/ticket/TCK-119

I’ll send the calendar invite now. Thanks again — we aim to have this fully verified and documented for your compliance audit by end of next week.

Best,
Irene
Sr. Technical Account Lead | Redwood Inference
(attachment: MAP-DataLine-verification-checklist.xlsx)
